analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 48-54) and docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 417). It documents a load-time 'shape warmup' for preloaded EngineV2 models, a new env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP (0/false/no/off disable; 'always' skips the probe), a 5-second sweep-tick warmup, and a 20s per-engine bound. Nothing executable, no auth, key, attestation, encryption, billing or coordinator-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance, examined and not found to regress:
- T-028 and T-041 (residual data in GPU memory, prefix-cache TTFT oracle): the docs say the warmup 'trains no rate or counter', is 'excluded', and uses a synthetic 128-token probe. Whether warmup touches the prefix cache, donates SSD blocks or reuses KV state cannot be checked from the docs. The implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, shapeWarmupMode) is not supplied.
- T-029 and T-010 (availability, idle GPU): idle-gated warmup that a request preempts is described. Preemption correctness is unverified.
- The env var is documented as forwarded to the LaunchAgent. This is an operator-controlled local knob and adds no consumer-reachable surface.

Remaining integration questions for deeper review, if the code change is in another batch: (1) warmup input must be synthetic and must never use consumer prompts or cache salts; (2) warmup must not populate or probe the encrypted SSD prefix cache or create at-rest artifacts outside the T-041 posture; (3) warmup must not delay coordinator challenge handling (the provider connection-control availability note); (4) a 20s-per-engine bound on a 5s sweep tick must not hold locks that block serving. These are unverified contracts, not findings.
